fixes.explanation: That one's True, friend. Peter writes that if you possess these qualities and continue to grow in them, “…they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” The qualities are the ones he just listed in verses 5 to 7, from virtue all the way up to love. I once squinted at a plain bowl of dough for ten minutes looking for a trick, and it was just dough. So the growing he asks for has a purpose: knowing Jesus in a way that isn't ineffective or unproductive.

Peter doesn't say life gets easier. What he says is, “…if you practice these things you will never stumble…” And look where he takes it next: “…you will receive a lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.” The promise points to where the road ends up, not to how smooth it is. I'd take steady feet over a smooth floor any day.
